hints.title: Concept
hints.body: Revenue is a per-line amount (price times quantity, reduced by the discount) that you then add up per product. Think row-level arithmetic first, group-level total second.

hints.title: Syntax or concept to use
hints.body: `SUM(...)` with `GROUP BY` collapses lines to one row per product. The discount is a fraction, so the kept share of a line is `1 - discount`. `ROUND(x, 2)` needs a numeric value in PostgreSQL.

hints.title: Approach
hints.body: Join `products` to `order_details`, compute the net amount from the order line's own price, quantity and discount, sum it per product, and sort the totals from largest to smallest.

hints.title: Structured steps
hints.body:
```sql
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name,
       ROUND(SUM(___)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue   -- net amount of each line
FROM products p
JOIN order_details od ON ___
GROUP BY ___
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
```
Every non-aggregated column in the SELECT list must also appear in GROUP BY.

debugging.symptom: Totals look too high for products that were often discounted.
debugging.cause: The `(1 - discount)` factor is missing, so each line counts at full price.
debugging.fix: Multiply the line amount by the share left after the discount.

debugging.symptom: `ERROR: column "p.product_name" must appear in the GROUP BY clause or be used in an aggregate function`.
debugging.cause: A selected column is neither aggregated nor listed in GROUP BY.
debugging.fix: Add every non-aggregated selected column to GROUP BY.

debugging.symptom: `ERROR: function round(double precision, integer) does not exist`.
debugging.cause: PostgreSQL only has two-argument ROUND for numeric values and this sum is a floating-point type.
debugging.fix: Cast the sum to numeric before rounding.

debugging.symptom: Revenue differs from the finance report when a product's list price changed over time.
debugging.cause: The query used `products.unit_price`, the current list price, instead of the price stored on each order line.

constraints: One row per product that has been ordered (an inner join).
Revenue is net of the line discount and rounded to 2 decimals.
sql:q01-product-revenue.realWorld: Product performance reviews and discontinuation decisions rest on net revenue per product, computed from the price actually charged on each order line.
commonMistakes: Counting lines (COUNT) when the question asks for money.
Using the current catalogue price for historical orders.
sql:q01-product-revenue.interviewRelevance: Revenue per product with a discount factor is a standard first aggregation question; the follow-up is usually products with no sales (a LEFT JOIN).
